title: Application-send turn campaign provenance architecture
purpose: Define a measurement-only provenance path for application-send turn forced-policy campaigns without conflating the existing receive-credit epoch stream with a second policy axis.
design_summary: Each forced application-send turn connection will emit one bounded, immutable construction-provenance record containing the canonical axis identifier, policy value, snapshot/rule version, connection pseudonym, and source linkage. The campaign host will retain that raw record beside host stdout confirmation, then join it to per-connection result evidence without changing receive-credit epoch rows. A result whose requested, host-reported, or connection-recorded identity disagrees is invalid_contract; a row with no eligible join remains retained with an explicit exclusion. The runtime record has no workload, peer, URL, application, or benchmark identity and has no policy consumer. Forced policy continues to bypass selection only, never scheduler validation or protocol safety guards.
alternatives_considered: Reuse receive-credit epoch snapshots as application-send records. Rejected because their rule, observations, and applied policy are attributable only to receive-credit publication.
Infer policy identity only from the host environment. Rejected because process-level confirmation cannot prove connection-local construction or a valid result-to-connection join.
Add a general online controller before campaigns. Rejected because the axis remains measurement-only and has no reviewed observation rule.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Legacy_current and conservative are closed values; unknown values fail campaign construction.
One construction record is emitted per connection without stream scans, per-packet allocation, global locking, or mutable policy state.
Missing, duplicate, stale, contradictory, or mismatched provenance is retained and classified; it is never repaired by relabeling or dropping rows.
Shadow is not introduced by this design; non-legacy forcing remains incompatible with the existing receive-credit shadow mode.
Adjacent axes remain legacy_current unless an independently reviewed factorial campaign says otherwise.
data_and_state_considerations: The new record is provenance, not an observation or a planner plan. It is immutable after connection construction, uses a pseudonymous campaign-local connection key, and can be emitted through a bounded sink. The local-result schema owns the axis-level forced/applied identity; normalized rows obtain their identity only through a checksum-verified join to the raw construction record. Receive-credit raw epochs and normalized rows retain their original axis provenance unchanged.
risks: A generic-looking event can invite future axis conflation; the record therefore carries an explicit canonical axis ID and a closed policy set.
A campaign result can appear complete despite missing joins; the validator must make missing or mismatched provenance ineligible rather than treating it as neutral.
Instrumentation could become a planner input; the record is write-only evidence and is not exposed to the planner interface.
